text:
sam: Heads up - multiple model-serving pods in eu-west-1 are failing to pull artifacts from the internal S3 endpoint after we rolled the interface endpoint change ~20m ago. Getting repeated TLS timeouts and `connection reset by peer` during streaming GETs.
lee: Oof. Are these failures only on certain subnets/AZs?
sam: Mostly subnet-03 and subnet-07 (gpu pool). Other subnets OK. Error from client: `curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer` on the vpc endpoint IPs.
anita: which endpoint did we create? s3, sts, or a proxy?
sam: We created an interface endpoint for S3 (vpce-0a1b2c3d) and switched DNS so requests resolve to the vpce. The ENIs are in the same subnets as the affected nodes.
lee: Can you `describe-network-interfaces` for the vpce ENIs and dump SGs?
sam: Ran `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters "Name=description,Values=*vpce-*" --region eu-west-1` and got ENIs with sg-0f1e2d3c attached.
lee: What are the egress rules on sg-0f1e2d3c?
sam: `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-0f1e2d3c` shows egress allow to 0.0.0.0/0 only on TCP 443. No ephemeral range allowed.
lee: aha. Interface endpoints are stateful - the endpoint SG controls traffic to the service ENI. If egress only allows 443, replies from the endpoint to client ephemeral ports will be blocked.
anita: But why only some subnets failing?
sam: Those subnets had an automation that replaced the default endpoint SG with our shared `endpoint-sg-prod` which is restricted to 443 only. Other subnets got the auto-generated endpoint SG that allows ephemeral.
lee: Can we confirm with a tcpdump on a failing node?
sam: ran `sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host 10.12.34.56 and tcp` (10.12.34.56 is a vpce ENI IP). See `SYN` -> `SYN,ACK` from endpoint -> then immediate `RST` from our node's port. Logs show `RST` for source ports > 1024.
anita: That matches blocked ephemeral replies. The endpoint SG is likely not allowing ephemeral outbound back to the caller. We need SG allowing ephemeral return traffic (1024-65535) from the vpce ENI to instances, or allow the instances to receive established responses.
lee: Quick fix: add egress rule to sg-0f1e2d3c for TCP 1024-65535 to the VPC CIDR. I can push a change.
sam: +1 please, it's causing model pulls to fail and resulting in retry storms.
infra-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-1432 - Interface endpoint egress policy blocking ephemeral port ranges (assigned to lee).
lee: Patching now: `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0f1e2d3c --protocol tcp --port 1024-65535 --cidr 10.0.0.0/8`
deploy-bot: Applied change via Terraform plan (module: vpce-endpoints, pr: #572).
anita: After the SG change, can you trigger a test pull?
sam: Retried a model download, streaming GET now completes, no resets. GPUs began pulling models again.
lee: Root cause: infra automation swapped the endpoint's auto SG for `endpoint-sg-prod` which had strict egress allowing only 443. That breaks TCP return path semantics for interface endpoints.
anita: Action items: 1) revert automation so it does not replace endpoint SGs by default 2) update `endpoint-sg-prod` to include ephemeral return range or a documented exception 3) add a check in infra-lint to detect vpce SGs without ephemeral egress allowed.
sam: Agree. Also adding an alert to monitoring when >5% of ECS tasks in a subnet have S3 pull errors in 1m.
infra-bot: Follow-up ticket created: INFRA-1729 (add infra-lint rule + alert).
lee: Leaving a short postmortem in #postmortems after we confirm no regressions.
sam: Thanks all - working now. :thumbsup:
